html:
The First Indochina War was the war of 1946 to 1954 in which the Viet Minh, the Communist-led independence front of Hồ Chí Minh, fought France for Vietnam. It ended French rule in Indochina.

After Japan surrendered in 1945, Hồ declared Vietnam independent in Hanoi. France came back in force, talks broke down, and fighting began in Hanoi in December 1946. The Viet Minh withdrew to the hills of Tonkin and fought a guerrilla war. After the Communists won China in 1949, Chinese aid reached the Viet Minh, and the United States paid a growing share of France's costs. A colonial war became part of the Cold War.

Võ Nguyên Giáp built the guerrillas into a regular army. In 1954 he surrounded the French base at Điện Biên Phủ, hauling artillery up the hills around it, and it fell on 7 May after 55 days. The Geneva Conference then split Vietnam at the 17th parallel, with Hồ's government in the North, where land reform followed. The split led to the Vietnam War.
